title: A week ago I said I'd cut voice acting from my LLM visual novel because TTS can't read the room. I put it back. Here's what changed and what it costs.
author: Defiant-Mood6717
selftext:
I'm the dev of Monte Lua, a browser visual novel where an LLM writes every page live (I posted about how the text, staging and pictures work here last week). In that post I said I'd removed character voices, because a voice that doesn't know the scene makes every line sound slightly wrong. This week voices went back in as an experimental option, so here's what was different the second time.

**The voice model never decides the delivery.** The first version sent raw lines to a TTS model and hoped. Now, once a page of prose is written, a small model (Haiku) reads the whole page and marks every spoken line: who says it, and how, as delivery tags the speech model understands (quiet, hesitant, laughing, a breath before the words). It also picks a voice for any side character who isn't part of the main cast. That pass costs about $0.003 per page and makes no audio.

**One line per request, just ahead of the reader.** The first build rendered a page's dialogue in one go, which pays for lines the player may never reach. Now the client asks only for the line on screen and the next spoken line. Each is one request to ElevenLabs v4 Turbo through OpenRouter and comes back in about 1 to 2 seconds, so the next line is usually ready before you click.

**Cost.** Turbo is $0.04 per 1,000 characters. The average spoken line is ~118 characters, so about half a cent a line. That's why voices are off by default and each voiced line costs the player one credit; the narration stays silent.

**Mixing mattered more than I expected.** With voices on, the music dips to half and the voice goes through a limiter, otherwise quiet lines vanished under the soundtrack. And if the player has muted the game or switched tabs, nothing is requested at all, so nobody pays for audio they can't hear.

**What I'm still not sure about:** whether a female player character should be voiced (we picked a voice, but the first three candidates all sounded like the cast), and whether anyone wants the narration read too.

Everything here is AI-made: the story, art, music and voices. If you want to hear it, it's free to start: https://montelua.ai/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=aigamedev-1125

Happy to answer questions about the pipeline.
